fields.title: Example Room
Shroud
fields.first_impression: A stack of 12 planks partly obscures the doorway. Beyond it stands a huge shrouded object about 9 feet tall.
contents: A stack of 12 planks partially obscures the doorway and appears to have boarded it up previously.
A huge shrouded object stands 9 feet tall.

discoverable.information: Removing the shroud reveals a guillotine with no blade and a winch on its side.
Turning the winch sounds and feels like a blade is being raised; after about 12 seconds the unseen mechanism falls with a heavy thunk.

hidden: The blade-less guillotine severs a victim's soul rather than the victim's head.
A severed soul is sent to room 99, which the source marks as not written yet.
triggers: Turning the winch starts a roughly 12-second cycle that ends with a heavy thunk.
A person whose head is in the guillotine when the cycle completes has their soul severed.
hazards: The guillotine can sever a person's soul without physically injuring the head or neck.

uncertainties.description: The destination is printed as room 99 followed by 'NOT WRITTEN YET', so no further destination details are available.

fields.title: Operate the Shroud Guillotine
fields.trigger: Someone turns the winch on the blade-less guillotine.
steps: Turn the winch; it sounds and feels as though a blade is being raised.
The unseen 'blade' falls with a heavy thunk.
If a person's head is in the guillotine at that moment, apply the soul-severance effect; the head and neck remain intact.

fields.title: Soul-Severing Guillotine Cycle
fields.perceived: After about 12 seconds of winching, the guillotine falls with a heavy thunk. A victim's head and neck remain physically intact, but the victim thereafter seems empty.

activation.condition: The guillotine cycle completes while someone has their head in it.

stakes: The victim's soul can be separated from the body.
A soulless victim can never level up again.
outcomes: The soul is sent to room 99 while the head and neck remain intact.
The victim gains the source's soulless immunities, detection anomalies, and empty behavior.
completion: The cycle ends when the guillotine falls with a heavy thunk.

uncertainties.description: Room 99 is explicitly marked 'NOT WRITTEN YET', so the soul's experience or recovery there is unspecified.

fields.title: Soul Severed by the Shroud Guillotine
fields.text: When the winched guillotine falls on someone whose head is in it, the victim's soul is severed and sent to room 99; the neck and head remain fully intact because there is no blade. A person without a soul is immune to mind reading, mind control, and emotions; does not detect as living, dead, or undead; sits down and stares at a wall whenever left alone; says they do not feel mindless but feel empty; and never levels up again.

uncertainties.description: The source provides no details for room 99 and marks it 'NOT WRITTEN YET'.

fields.title: Stone Egg
fields.first_impression: A ravenous ghoul shares the room with a polished pinkish-brown stone egg about 3 feet tall, covered in grooves, whorls, and carved animals.
contents: A polished pinkish-brown stone egg about 3 feet tall, covered with grooves, whorls, and carved animals.
The carvings depict an ape, elephant, bat, chicken, snake, octopus, rat, pyorn (giant bird), horse, and toad.

discoverable.information: Faint screaming can be heard from inside the Stone Egg.
discoverable.condition: Put an ear against the egg.

discoverable.information: Each animal carving lights up when touched.
The egg unfolds like a flower when the chicken, snake, octopus, pyorn, and toad are touched simultaneously.
discoverable.condition: Experiment with the carvings or identify and touch all egg-laying animals at once.

discoverable.information: Every five incorrect animal touches makes the glow of a touched animal dimmer; after four failed attempts the egg becomes inert for 24 hours.
discoverable.condition: Accumulate incorrect inputs while testing the carvings.

hidden: The egg is Shawson the ghoul's prison.
Inside are 600 silver shilavos, the Abacus of Vandoh, a head that never stops screaming, and a headless skeleton.
Climbing inside causes the egg to zip shut and trap the entrant until suffocation; the corpse becomes a perpetually screaming head attached to a skeleton.
triggers: Touching all five egg-laying animal carvings simultaneously opens the egg.
Each five incorrect animal touches advances the failure track; after four failed attempts the egg is inert for 24 hours.
Opening the egg fills the air with screaming and provokes an Encounter check.
Climbing inside the opened egg causes it to zip shut.
hazards: The egg can trap and suffocate anyone who climbs inside.

fields.title: Shawson the Ghoul
fields.role: A ravenous, insane ghoul imprisoned in the Stone Egg room.
goals: Kill the person he currently calls his 'pretty little fish'.
behavior: Calls his intended victim his 'pretty little fish' and calls everyone else a 'dirty filthy'.
capabilities: Move as human; Int 5; Str 7; Dis hungry.
starting_state: Trying to kill his 'pretty little fish'.

uncertainties.description: The source does not identify which person Shawson means by his 'pretty little fish'.

fields.title: Shawson's Agony
fields.text: Shawson's claw attack is printed as 'Claw 1d6+agony'.

uncertainties.description: This page names the added 'agony' effect but does not define its mechanics.

fields.title: Open the Stone Egg
fields.trigger: Someone interacts with the Stone Egg's animal carvings.
steps: Touching any animal carving makes it light up.
Touch the five egg-laying animals—chicken, snake, octopus, pyorn, and toad—simultaneously.
On the correct simultaneous input, the egg unfolds like a flower.
Each set of five incorrect animal touches makes the glow of a touched animal dimmer.
After four failed attempts, the egg becomes inert for 24 hours before it can be tried again.

fields.title: The Stone Egg Opens
fields.perceived: The carved stone egg unfolds like a flower and the sound of screaming fills the air.

activation.condition: The chicken, snake, octopus, pyorn, and toad carvings are touched simultaneously.

repeat.condition: Attempts can continue until it opens, but four failed attempts make it inert for 24 hours.

stakes: The screaming provokes an Encounter check.
Anyone who climbs inside can be sealed in and suffocated.
approaches: Identify and touch all five egg-laying animal carvings simultaneously.
outcomes: The egg opens and exposes 600 silver shilavos, the Abacus of Vandoh, a perpetually screaming head, and a headless skeleton.
A person who climbs inside is trapped until suffocation and transformed into a perpetually screaming head attached to a skeleton.
completion: The egg unfolds like a flower after the correct simultaneous input.

fields.title: Stone Egg Entrapment and Screaming-Head Transformation
fields.text: If anyone climbs inside the Stone Egg, it zips back up and traps that person until death by suffocation. At death, the victim becomes a perpetually screaming head attached to a skeleton.

fields.title: 600 Silver Shilavos
fields.text: A cache of 600 silver shilavos is inside the opened Stone Egg.

fields.title: Abacus of Vandoh
fields.text: A Treasure called the Abacus of Vandoh is inside the opened Stone Egg; the source points to Appendix A for its full description.

uncertainties.description: The item's Appendix A mechanics are not present on this page.

fields.title: Perpetually Screaming Head
fields.text: The opened Stone Egg contains a severed head that never stops screaming. A person killed by entrapment in the egg also becomes a perpetually screaming head attached to a skeleton.

fields.title: Ghost Fence
fields.first_impression: A line of 30 rotten severed heads divides the east and west sides of the room. Above them, 30 hands hang from a rope stretched north to south.
contents: Thirty severed heads arranged as a barrier, alternating the directions they face; their yellow eyes look wet and alive.
Thirty hands dangling directly above the heads from a 30-foot rope held by two iron spikes between the north and south walls.
The rope and hands are entirely non-magical.

discoverable.information: Moving any head out of the specific formation ends the fence's effects; returning the heads to formation restores them.
discoverable.condition: Move at least one head out of formation and observe the result.

discoverable.information: The heads can be moved elsewhere and reassembled to recreate the effect.
discoverable.condition: Remove and later restore the heads in their specific formation.

hidden: Touching the heads or passing over them kills the nearest living thing with no Save.
triggers: The heads continuously stare at the nearest living or undead creature and make that target chatter its teeth.
Touching a head or passing over the formation triggers instant death for the nearest living thing.
Restoring the specific head formation reactivates the effects.
hazards: The nearest targeted creature chatters its teeth uncontrollably.
Touching or crossing over the heads can kill the nearest living thing with no Save.

fields.title: Disrupt the Ghost Fence
fields.trigger: The party needs to pass or neutralize the severed-head formation.
steps: Move at least one severed head out of its specific formation.
While the formation is broken, the fence's magical effects end.
Cross or move the heads as needed; the source suggests bowling with isopods as an easy way past.
If the heads are returned to their specific formation, the effects resume, even if the formation is rebuilt elsewhere.

fields.title: Crossing the Ghost Fence
fields.perceived: The wet-eyed severed heads stare at the nearest creature and chatter their teeth; the watched creature's own teeth chatter uncontrollably.

activation.condition: The 30 heads remain in their specific formation.

repeat.condition: The effects resume whenever the formation is restored.

stakes: Touching the heads or passing over them kills the nearest living thing with no Save.
approaches: Move one or more heads out of formation.
Use isopods like bowling balls to get past the barrier; the source notes that many solutions exist.
outcomes: Breaking the formation ends the effects.
Restoring the formation reactivates the effects, even at a different location.
completion: The party crosses while the formation is disrupted, or permanently leaves the heads out of formation.

fields.title: Ghost Fence Chattering
fields.text: While the heads are in formation, they stare at the nearest creature, living or undead, and chatter their teeth. The creature they stare at also chatters its teeth uncontrollably.

fields.title: Ghost Fence Instant Death and Formation Dependence
fields.text: If the heads are touched or someone passes over them, the nearest living thing dies with no Save. Moving any head out of the specific formation ends the effect; returning the heads to formation restores it. The heads can be transported and set up elsewhere with the same effect.

fields.title: Sunken Shrine
fields.first_impression: A shrine chamber lies under 10 feet of water, with several submerged stone and metal forms visible below the surface.

discoverable.information: Four stone pews, a rusted metal cage large enough to hold a person, a stone idol of Vandoh, and a quadrupedal statue lie beneath the water.

The Vandoh statue is a polished marble muscular male in a toga, rendered in polygons with time-smoothed vertices; its platonic-solid head seems to have a different number of sides each time it is counted.
discoverable.condition: Examine the stone idol of Vandoh.

hidden: The quadrupedal statue is an ancient apparatus of anguish made of pinkish-brown stone, grooves, and whorls.
Four feet of water above the apparatus's head protects it from falling bricks.
Two rounds after someone enters, the apparatus attacks and tries to exit the pit.
The first person to speak or pray to the Vandoh statue has their left hand possessed.
triggers: Two rounds after anyone enters the room, the ancient apparatus attempts to attack and leave the pit.
The first person to speak or pray to the Vandoh statue triggers left-hand possession.
hazards: The submerged ancient apparatus attacks intruders with its slam and Ancient Tone.
occupants: An ancient apparatus of anguish disguised externally as a quadrupedal statue.

fields.title: Ancient Apparatus of Anguish
fields.appearance: A quadrupedal statue without a clear head or face, made of pinkish-brown stone and covered in whorls and grooves.
fields.role: A submerged ancient killing apparatus that activates after intruders enter, attacks them, and tries to escape the shrine pit.
goals: Exit the pit and escape the room.
behavior: Begins attacking two rounds after someone enters the room.
Its gaze makes skin-covered, large-dice-sized cubes of a fleshy target fall away without pain, leaving healthy skin over the wounds and a sudden numb sensation.
capabilities: Stone — All non-bludgeoning damage is reduced to 1.
Ancient Tone — A fleshy target within 10 feet takes 1d6 damage; a Cha Save negates.
Anguish Pattern — Whenever this apparatus damages something with its tone, all ancient apparatuses within 30 feet, including itself, are healed for an equal amount.
Four feet of water above its head protects it from falling bricks.

reactions.stimulus: The apparatus loses half of its hit points.
reactions.response: It begins bleeding, revealing that it is only a statue on the outside, and attempts to escape the room.

hidden: It is only a statue on the outside; it bleeds after losing half its hit points.

fields.title: Ancient Apparatus Awakening
fields.perceived: Two rounds after someone enters, the submerged quadrupedal statue begins attacking and tries to climb out of the pit. At half hit points it starts bleeding despite its stone exterior.

activation.condition: Two rounds after someone enters the Sunken Shrine, whether by falling or another route.

participants.role: Attacks intruders and attempts to escape.

actor_reactions.reaction: On losing half its hit points, it begins bleeding and attempts to escape the room.

stakes: Intruders face slam and Ancient Tone damage.
An escaping apparatus may become a wandering monster.
outcomes: If it escapes, it can be added to the wandering monster table.

possible_effects.description: An escaped ancient apparatus can be added to the wandering monster table.

fields.title: Stone
fields.text: All non-bludgeoning damage dealt to the ancient apparatus of anguish is reduced to 1.

fields.title: Ancient Tone
fields.text: A fleshy target within 10 feet takes 1d6 damage; a Cha Save negates. The apparatus's gaze makes parts of the target fall away as skin-covered cubes about the size of large dice. The resulting wounds are covered with healthy skin; there is no pain, only sudden numbness.

fields.title: Anguish Pattern
fields.text: Whenever the apparatus damages something with its tone, every ancient apparatus within 30 feet, including this one, is healed for an amount equal to the damage dealt.

fields.title: Vandoh Possesses a Left Hand
fields.perceived: The first speaker or supplicant's left hand becomes rigid and holds up a number of fingers. It clenches with rage whenever a ghoul is encountered.

activation.condition: The first person speaks or prays to the statue of Vandoh.

stakes: A character's left hand is possessed and rigid.
outcomes: The raised finger count equals the number of ghouls remaining in the dungeon.
The hand clenches with rage whenever a ghoul is encountered.
If all ghouls are killed, the character becomes Favored by Vandoh.
completion: Killing all ghouls triggers the character becoming Favored by Vandoh.

possible_effects.description: If all ghouls are killed, the possessed character becomes Favored by Vandoh as described in Appendix D.

fields.title: Vandoh's Possessed Left Hand
fields.text: The first person to speak or pray to the statue has their left hand possessed. The hand is rigid and holds up a number of fingers equal to the number of ghouls remaining in the dungeon. Whenever a ghoul is encountered, the hand clenches with rage.

fields.title: Favored by Vandoh
fields.text: If all ghouls are killed, the character whose left hand was possessed becomes Favored by Vandoh; the source points to Appendix D for the full effect.

uncertainties.description: The mechanics of Favored by Vandoh are not present on this page and are deferred to Appendix D.

fields.title: Stone Idol of Vandoh
fields.text: A stone idol of Vandoh rises from the water in 41 SUNKEN SHRINE. The first person to speak or pray to it has their left hand possessed; the hand holds up a number of fingers equal to the ghouls remaining in the dungeon and clenches when a ghoul is encountered.

fields.title: Sunken Gallery
fields.first_impression: A 40-foot-tall gallery lies under 10 feet of water. Six huge statues loom from the pool, each holding a stone coffer.
contents: Six huge statues, each with an integral stone coffer that cannot be removed.
A proud king holds his coffer overhead and gazes at the shepherd.
A weary knight watches the crone.
A smiling shepherd with a sheep under one arm watches the scribe.
A beggar extends a plate toward the crone.
A crone bows to the king and holds her coffer behind her back.
A scribe watches the crone while clutching a scroll to his chest.

discoverable.information: The scribe's scroll reads: 'The sheep do not know the shepherd, but they follow nonetheless'.
discoverable.condition: Read the scroll clutched by the scribe statue.

hidden: The king, knight, shepherd, beggar, and scribe coffers contain poisonous gas.
The crone's coffer contains the hand mirror of lies, a bottle of liquid boat, and a pouch of 50 golden gorbels worth 500s.
The room connects to 24 CRUSH HALLWAY and 25 TRICKY HALLWAY, but neither can be accessed unless its trap door is open.
triggers: Opening a poison-filled coffer exposes anyone in front of it to a Dex save against poisoning and then releases gas that fills the room.
Open trap doors permit access to 24 CRUSH HALLWAY and 25 TRICKY HALLWAY.
hazards: Five coffers contain poison gas that expands to fill the room and takes 10 minutes to settle.
resources: A pouch containing 50 golden gorbels, worth 500s.

fields.title: The Scribe's Scroll
fields.text: The scroll clutched by the scribe statue reads: 'The sheep do not know the shepherd, but they follow nonetheless'.

fields.title: Handle a Sunken Gallery Coffer
fields.trigger: Someone opens one of the statues' stone coffers.
steps: Opening a poison-filled coffer forces anyone in front of it to make a Dex save or become poisoned for 1d6 damage per round until a Con check succeeds.
Opening with a hooked pole or from the side grants a +4 bonus to the Dex check.
After opening, the poison gas expands to fill the room.
Characters who flee immediately are not poisoned by the expanding gas.
The poison gas settles after 10 minutes.

uncertainties.description: The source first calls the avoidance roll a Dex save and later calls the roll receiving the +4 bonus a Dex check.

fields.title: Poison Coffer Discharge
fields.perceived: A poison-filled coffer releases gas from its front and the cloud expands through the gallery.

activation.condition: Any of the five poison-filled coffers is opened.

repeat.condition: The hazard can trigger from each poison-filled coffer.

stakes: Anyone in front of the coffer risks ongoing poison damage.
The expanding gas can poison characters who do not flee immediately.
approaches: Open the coffer with a hooked pole or from the side for a +4 bonus.
Flee immediately when the gas begins to fill the room.
outcomes: A failed Dex save poisons a character for 1d6 damage per round until a Con check succeeds.
Immediate flight avoids poisoning from the room-filling cloud.
completion: The gas settles 10 minutes after release.

uncertainties.description: The page uses both 'Dex save' and 'Dex check' for the same coffer-opening defense.

fields.title: Sunken Gallery Poison Gas
fields.text: When a poison-filled coffer is opened, anyone in front must make a Dex save or be poisoned for 1d6 damage per round until a Con check succeeds. A hooked pole or opening from the side grants +4 to the Dex check. The gas then fills the room; characters who flee immediately are not poisoned, and the gas takes 10 minutes to settle.

uncertainties.description: The source alternates between the terms Dex save and Dex check for the avoidance roll.

fields.title: Hand Mirror of Lies
fields.text: The crone's coffer contains the hand mirror of lies, a Treasure whose full description is in Appendix A.

uncertainties.description: The item's Appendix A mechanics are not present on this page.

fields.title: Bottle of Liquid Boat
fields.text: The crone's coffer contains a bottle of liquid boat; the source points to Appendix A for its full description.

uncertainties.description: The item's Appendix A mechanics are not present on this page.

fields.title: Pouch of 50 Golden Gorbels
fields.text: The crone's coffer contains a pouch holding 50 golden gorbels, valued at 500s.

fields.title: Spider Crab
fields.first_impression: A pool of unusually murky brown water lies 10 feet deep, with the floor above 40 feet above the water's surface.
contents: Brown water 10 feet deep and much murkier than usual.

discoverable.information: A giant spider crab is watching from the water with its eyestalks near the surface.
discoverable.condition: Notice the eyestalks or otherwise detect the hidden crab.

hidden: A giant undead spider crab hides in the water.
The crab is all that remains of a high priestess of Vandoh.
The crab can reach 38 feet out of the water, two feet short of the floor above.
If a large object is dropped into the pool, the crab eventually uses it as a platform to escape.
triggers: The first time the crab notices that it has been noticed, it hides for a few seconds.
Anything dropped within its 38-foot reach causes it to lunge.
Dropping a large object such as a table or ballista into the pool eventually lets the crab stand on it and escape.
hazards: The hidden giant undead spider crab lunges at anything that falls within reach.
occupants: A giant undead spider crab, formerly a high priestess of Vandoh.

fields.title: Spider Crab
fields.appearance: A giant undead spider crab that keeps its eyestalks above the murky water to watch the party.
fields.role: A hidden pool predator and the remains of a high priestess of Vandoh; if it escapes, it becomes a wandering monster.
goals: Lunge at anything that drops within reach.
Escape the pit when given a large object to stand on.
behavior: Tries to keep its eyestalks above water while watching the party.
The first time it realizes it has been noticed, it tries to hide for a few seconds.
Eventually stands on any large object dropped in the pool and escapes.
capabilities: Can reach 38 feet out of the water.

reactions.stimulus: It first notices that the party has noticed it.
reactions.response: It tries to hide for a few seconds.
It lunges at the falling object or creature.

reactions.stimulus: A large object such as a table or ballista is dropped into the pool.
reactions.response: It eventually stands on the object and escapes the pit.

hidden: It is all that remains of a high priestess of Vandoh.
starting_state: Hiding in the water and watching the party with its eyestalks above the surface.

fields.title: Spider Crab in the Pool
fields.perceived: Eyestalks watch from the murky water. When noticed, they dip away for a few seconds; anything falling close enough draws a sudden lunge from the pool.

activation.condition: The giant undead spider crab remains hidden in the pool while creatures or objects are within the room.

repeat.condition: The crab can lunge whenever something drops within its 38-foot reach.

participants.role: Watches from hiding, lunges at falling targets, and seeks a way out.

actor_reactions.reaction: The first time it knows it has been seen, it hides for a few seconds.
It lunges at anything dropped within its reach.
It uses a large dropped object as a platform and eventually escapes.

stakes: Anything falling within 38 feet of the surface can be attacked and grabbed.
A large dropped object can release the crab into the dungeon.
approaches: Avoid dropping creatures or objects within the crab's reach.
Recognize that a large object in the pool will let the crab climb out.
outcomes: The crab lunges at a falling target.
If a large object is dropped into the pool, the crab eventually escapes and is added to the wandering monster table.
completion: The crab escapes the pit after gaining a large object to stand on.

possible_effects.description: After escaping, the spider crab is added to the wandering monster table.

fields.title: Spider Crab Grab
fields.text: The spider crab's attack line is printed as 'Claw/claw 1d8/1d8+grab', so its second claw attack adds a grab effect.

uncertainties.description: This page names the grab rider but does not define its procedure, duration, escape condition, or other mechanics.

fields.perceived: A player-safe description of what happens.
stakes: What the source says is at risk.
fields.title: Example Standoff
